F1.quote: Labor Notes is a media and organizing project that has been the voice of union activists who want to put the movement back in the labor movement since 1979.
F1.claim: a media and organizing project, the voice since 1979 of union activists who want to put the movement back in the labor movement
F1.lineage: what it is: a media and organizing project, the voice of union activists

F2.quote: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local … October 29, 2026 / Sarah Hughes
F2.claim: its lead story on 31 October 2026: members alarmed by an end-run around democracy at a Buffalo health care local

F3.quote: UFCW Members Protect Local Election After Sham Merger Attempt … October 26, 2026 / Lisa Xu
F3.claim: a current story: UFCW members protect a local election after a sham merger attempt

F4.quote: State Workers Strike Across California … October 28, 2026 / Kari Thompson
F4.claim: a current story: state workers strike across California

F5.quote: Mailing Address: 55 Washington St, Suite 522, Brooklyn, NY 11201
F5.claim: its mailing address is in Brooklyn, NY

F6.claim: the footer's copyright holder is the Labor Education and Research Project, © 2005-2023

F7.quote: Labor Notes is a monthly magazine that supports union organizing and collective bargaining in the United States.
F7.claim: a monthly magazine that supports union organizing and collective bargaining in the United States

F8.quote: It is published by the Labor Education and Research Project, an American non-profit organization and network for rank-and-file union members and grassroots labor activists.
F8.claim: published by the Labor Education and Research Project, a non-profit organization and network for rank-and-file members and grassroots activists

F9.quote: The magazine reports news and analysis about labor activity and issues facing the labor movement. It promotes a revitalization of the labor movement through social movement unionism and union democracy.
F9.claim: it reports labor news and analysis and promotes revitalization through social movement unionism and union democracy
F9.lineage: what it promotes: organizing and member-run unions

F10.quote: Labor Notes is based in Detroit, Michigan, with an East Coast office in Brooklyn, New York.
F10.claim: based in Detroit, with an East Coast office in Brooklyn

F11.quote: It grew from a strategy by labor activists who sought to build grassroots connections across unions and industries. It works to bridge the gap between isolated rank-and-file caucuses and reform groups. The most notable example is Teamsters for a Democratic Union.
F11.claim: it bridges isolated rank-and-file caucuses and reform groups, Teamsters for a Democratic Union the most notable example

F12.quote: Labor Notes was launched to help strengthen those linkages following the Bituminous Coal Strike of 1977–1978 and the cross-union solidarity it generated.
F12.claim: launched after the Bituminous Coal Strike of 1977–1978 to strengthen cross-union linkages

F13.quote: First issue March 1979 … Company Labor Education and Research Project
F13.claim: first issue March 1979; company the Labor Education and Research Project

F14.quote: In 1982, the first Labor Notes conference, Organizing Against Concessions, brought together hundreds of activists. In 1983, Labor Notes published one of its first books, Concessions and How to Beat Them by Jane Slaughter.
F14.claim: the first conference in 1982 (Organizing Against Concessions); an early book in 1983 (Slaughter), a sentence the article marks 'citation needed'
F14.mark: the article marks the 1983 sentence '[citation needed]' (December 2025)

F15.quote: It opposed the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and published Unions and Free Trade by Kim Moody and Mary McGinn in 1992
F15.claim: it opposed NAFTA and published Unions and Free Trade by Kim Moody and Mary McGinn in 1992

F16.quote: Its best-known titles include A Troublemaker’s Handbook: How to Fight Back Where You Work and Win by Dan La Botz, published in 1991, … Another widely used book is Democracy is Power: Rebuilding Unions from the Bottom Up, by Mike Parker and Martha Gruelle.
F16.claim: its best-known books: A Troublemaker’s Handbook (La Botz, 1991) and its sequel; Democracy is Power (Parker and Gruelle)

F17.quote: Every two years, Labor Notes holds a national conference that brings together more than a thousand union members and leaders from the United States, Canada, Mexico, and other countries. The purpose of these conferences is to help activists build networks based on shared issues. The most recent such conference was in June, 2026.
F17.claim: a national conference every two years, more than a thousand members and leaders from several countries, to build networks on shared issues; the most recent in June 2026

F18.quote: This article is about the magazine. For the alternative currency, see Labour voucher.
F18.claim: the article is about the magazine; 'Labour voucher' (the alternative currency) is another entity
F18.lineage: the encyclopedia's own notices and the homonym

F19.quote: This article contains promotional content. … This article needs more citations.
F19.claim: the article carries its own notices: promotional content; more citations needed (April 2025)
F19.lineage: the encyclopedia's own notices and the homonym
F19.note: the encyclopedia's own maintenance notices, April 2025

F20.quote: As immigrant workers centers grew as new forms of worker self-organization, Labor Notes covered these developments and brought their leaders together at its bi-annual conference.
F20.claim: it covered immigrant worker centers and brought their leaders together at its conference

F21.claim: a card titled with the name and Brooklyn NY

F22.quote: Labor Notes Conferences are the biggest gatherings of grassroots union activists, union reformers, and all-around troublemakers out there!
F22.claim: its conferences: the biggest gatherings of grassroots union activists, union reformers and troublemakers

F23.quote: More than 200 meetings and workshops include creative organizing tactics, beating apathy, running for local union office, winning contract campaigns, bargaining over technology, assertive grievance handling, and reviving the strike.
F23.claim: more than 200 meetings and workshops in 2024, from running for local union office to reviving the strike

F24.quote: Face-to-face meetings to share tactics and swap notes are the heart of the Labor Notes Conference. Join an existing industry, union, or caucus meeting—or contact us to set one up.
F24.claim: face-to-face meetings, among them caucus meetings, are the heart of the conference

F25.quote: 2024 Labor Notes Conference: April 19-21 … This will be the largest conference we've ever had … WHERE: Hyatt Regency O'Hare, Rosemont (Chicago), Illinois
F25.claim: the 2024 conference, April 19-21 at the Hyatt Regency O'Hare in Rosemont, registration closed, 'the largest conference we've ever had'

F26.quote: Labor news from labor's point of view. $30 for 11 issues.
F26.claim: the magazine by subscription, $30 for 11 issues

F27.quote: Labor Network for Sustainability joined thousands of rank-and-file workers, organizers, and union leaders at the 2024 Labor Notes conference last month
F27.claim: the Labor Network for Sustainability joined thousands of rank-and-file workers, organizers and leaders at the 2024 conference
F27.date: 2024-05 (the month after the April 2024 conference, by its own 'last month')

F28.quote: LNS also helped facilitate a Climate Change and Labor meetup building on conversations from the last Labor Notes conference
F28.claim: LNS facilitated a Climate Change and Labor meetup at the conference
F28.date: 2024-05 (the month after the April 2024 conference, by its own 'last month')

F29.quote: For four decades Labor Notes has offered activists a ringside view of labor's ups and downs.
F29.claim: for four decades a ringside view of labor's ups and downs

F30.quote: Whether we're reporting on a struggle across the street or around the world, Labor Notes delivers the best labor news and analysis available.
F30.claim: it reports struggles near and abroad and calls its news and analysis the best available

F31.quote: Labor Notes is a nonprofit organization founded in 1979 as a publication and movement hub that offers training and resources for rank-and-file union members to build the labor movement through workplace organizing and democratizing unions.
F31.claim: a participant's definition: a nonprofit founded in 1979 as a publication and movement hub for rank-and-file members, organizing workplaces and democratizing unions
F31.lineage: what it is: a media and organizing project, the voice of union activists

F32.quote: This year’s conference was the biggest ever, with over 4,700 attendees
F32.claim: the 2024 conference the biggest ever, over 4,700 attendees, by a participant's count

F33.quote: I’ve heard many people credit Labor Notes and its popular book Secrets of a Successful Organizer with helping them succeed in organizing their workplace or taking on other organizing challenges.
F33.claim: a participant reports many crediting Labor Notes and Secrets of a Successful Organizer with their organizing

F34.quote: Content published does not necessarily reflect the views of Metro DC DSA or the national DSA.
F34.claim: the publication's own limit: its content does not necessarily reflect Metro DC DSA's or national DSA's views
F34.lineage: the encyclopedia's own notices and the homonym

F35.quote: the Labor Notes Conference June 12-14 in Chicago was an oasis of inspiration and solidarity. … This year’s 300 workshops and panels
F35.claim: the 2026 conference, June 12-14 in Chicago, with 300 workshops and panels

F36.quote: At the heart of the conference each year are sectoral meetings, where workers meet up with others in the same industry from different locations and unions.
F36.claim: sectoral meetings across unions are at the heart of each conference

F37.quote: Labor Notes gives workers a rare chance to come together across unions, sectors, and identities.
F37.claim: it gives workers a chance to meet across unions, sectors and identities

F38.quote: Putting the movement back in the labor movement since 1979. … Detroit, MI … Joined February 2009
F38.claim: its X profile: 'Putting the movement back in the labor movement since 1979', location Detroit, MI, joined February 2009

F39.quote: An insurgent slate is challenging longtime incumbents in Local 8-Golden State, one of the largest locals in the United Food and Commercial Workers, in what may be the local’s first competitive election in decades
F39.claim: a post on an insurgent slate challenging longtime incumbents in UFCW Local 8-Golden State

F40.quote: "Every single time that you get frustrated or you run into a wall, someone from Labor Notes is going to be there to pick you up," Nora Meek, a founding member of the IATSE CREW reform caucus, says in our new video.
F40.claim: a founding member of the IATSE CREW reform caucus on the support Labor Notes gives

F41.quote: October 22, 2025 / Kate Bronfenbrenner … [This article is part of a Labor Notes roundtable series: How Can Unions Defend Worker Power Against Trump 2.0?
F41.claim: an article of 22 October 2025 by Kate Bronfenbrenner in its roundtable series on defending worker power against Trump 2.0

F42.quote: Difficult as it may be, unions must organize workers in the nation’s largest and most powerful corporations, and they cannot afford to wait for labor law reform or a more favorable administration to do so.
F42.claim: Bronfenbrenner's argument: unions must organize the largest corporations without waiting for law reform

F43.quote: June 22, 2022 / Alexandra Bradbury … Thank you to all 4,000 troublemakers who converged in Chicago June 17-19 and made this year's Labor Notes Conference incredible.

F44.quote: The main sessions, a few of the biggest panels, and the concert were livestreamed and are now available in video form.
F44.claim: its main 2022 sessions livestreamed and kept as video

F45.quote: Through our magazine, website, books, conferences, and workshops, we promote organizing, aggressive strategies to take on employers, labor-community solidarity, and unions that are run by their members.
F45.claim: what it promotes: organizing, aggressive strategies against employers, labor-community solidarity, unions run by their members
F45.lineage: what it promotes: organizing and member-run unions
F45.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; its conference notice predates June 2026)

F46.quote: Labor Notes is also a network of rank-and-file members, local union leaders, and labor activists who know the labor movement is worth fighting for. We encourage connections between workers in different unions, worker centers, communities, industries, and countries to strengthen the movement—from the bottom up.
F46.claim: also a network of rank-and-file members, local leaders and activists, encouraging connections across unions and countries 'from the bottom up'
F46.lineage: what it promotes: organizing and member-run unions
F46.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; its conference notice predates June 2026)

F47.quote: For the most part, our leaders are doing a poor job of navigating us through the crisis. Some can’t get beyond business-as-usual; others see the need to organize by the millions, but don't believe that workers themselves need to have a say in their unions.
F47.claim: its critique of union leaders: a poor job through the crisis; business-as-usual; workers given no say
F47.lineage: critique of union leaderships and independence
F47.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; its conference notice predates June 2026)

F48.quote: With 45 years of movement building behind us, Labor Notes exists as a resource for leaders and union members who want to combat these trends and chart a new course for the labor movement.
F48.claim: it exists as a resource for those who want to combat these trends and chart a new course
F48.lineage: critique of union leaderships and independence
F48.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; its conference notice predates June 2026)

F49.quote: Labor Notes is best known for our monthly magazine of the same name. We report news about workers that the mainstream media doesn't find worth printing—from workers’ point of view.
F49.claim: best known for its monthly magazine, which reports news about workers from workers' point of view
F49.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; its conference notice predates June 2026)

F50.quote: And as an independent publication, we’re free to include the voices who say we could be doing better—and tell how.
